- **Interface-First Design**: Define contracts before implementations

- **State Externalization**: Game state lives in structured data, not context

# Architecture

Memory Reconstruction separates **rules** from **presentation**. The simulation
(`src/sim`) is plain TypeScript with no DOM or PixiJS imports. Everything else
reads its state and reacts to the events it emits. See ADR-016 in
`.aikit/decisions.md` for why the earlier module-registry design was replaced.

```text
             InputFrame (one per 1/60 s step)
  input/ ───────────────────────────────┐
                                        ▼
                               ┌──────────────────┐
                               │  sim/World.step  │  deterministic, seeded
                               └───────┬──────────┘
                    SimEvent[]         │        state (read-only)
          ┌────────────────┬───────────┼──────────────┬─────────────┐
          ▼                ▼           ▼              ▼             ▼
     view/Renderer    audio/Sound   ui/Hud     app/App (flow)   save/SaveStore
     (PixiJS)         (Web Audio)   (DOM)      title/pause/      (localStorage)
                                               choice/death
```

## Frame loop (`app/App.ts`)

1. Read the gamepad, then run as many fixed 1/60 s simulation steps as real
   time allows (up to 5 per frame; the backlog is dropped after that).
2. Before each step, `Renderer.beforeStep()` records positions. Each step
   turns input into an `InputFrame`, calls `World.step`, and passes the
   returned events to the renderer, sound, HUD and the App's own flow
   handling (floor exit, death, victory, fragment saving).
3. Render once, interpolating positions between the last two steps, then
   update the HUD.

The App is a state machine: `title → playing ⇄ paused | choice | map →
transition → playing … → dead | victory → title`.

## Simulation (`src/sim`)

| Module         | Responsibility                                                                 |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `rng.ts`       | mulberry32 RNG; `floorSeed(runSeed, depth)` gives each floor its own seed       |
| `tiles.ts`     | `TileGrid`: void/floor/wall/door tiles, decorations, locked doors              |
| `dungeon.ts`   | floor generator: rooms on a 6x6 cell grid, straight 3-wide corridors, room kinds |
| `physics.ts`   | box-versus-tile movement with sub-steps and corner slipping; circle separation  |
| `pathing.ts`   | flow field toward the player so enemies route around pillars                   |
| `content.ts`   | typed views of `enemies.json`, `biomes.json`, `lore.json`; the floor plan       |
| `entities.ts`  | plain-data `Player`, `Enemy`, `Projectile`, `Pickup`, `Interactable`, `InputFrame` |
| `combat.ts`    | the `Arena` interface actors use, plus arc and damage helpers                  |
| `player.ts`    | movement, three-hit combo, dash, bolt, potion                                   |
| `enemies.ts`   | archetype AI (melee, skirmisher, caster, brute, boss) with windup telegraphs    |
| `upgrades.ts`  | upgrade cards; stats are recomputed from the counts taken                      |
| `run.ts`       | `RunState` carried across floors: XP, level-ups, choices, save/restore          |
| `world.ts`     | one floor in play: rooms, waves, loot, projectiles, interactables, `step()`     |

Rules that matter when changing the sim:

- **Determinism.** All randomness goes through the World's `Rng`. Same seed
  plus same inputs gives the same result (tested).
- **Plain data.** Entities and `RunState` are JSON-serializable. A save is
  `JSON.stringify(run)`, and `restoreRun` recomputes derived stats.
- **No import of `world.ts` from actors.** Player and enemy code see only the
  `Arena` interface, which keeps the module graph acyclic.
- **Fairness.** Enemies hurt only through telegraphed attacks: windup, then
  attack, then a recovery window the player can punish.

### Floors

`FLOOR_PLANS` in `content.ts` fixes six floors: biome, enemy roster, boss and
room count. The last is a straight approach to the Keeper's arena. Every room
contains its cell's centre band, so corridors run straight along cell centre
lines and never cut through another room. Obstacles stay off the centre lines,
which keeps every doorway reachable (tested across seeds).

Entering a combat or boss room (fully past its doorway) locks its doors and
spawns waves. Clearing it unlocks the doors. The treasure room holds a chest
(upgrade pick plus a memory fragment), the shrine holds a Memory Well (shards
buy healing and a pick), and the boss drops a fragment and opens the exit rift.

## View (`src/view`)

- `Renderer.ts`: the PixiJS application, layer stack, camera (smooth follow,
  aim look-ahead, shake, height-based zoom), darkness vignette, hurt flash.
- `LevelView.ts`: tile sprites in 16x16-tile chunks, culled off-screen. Wall
  faces show where a wall has floor to its south, with caps above for height.
  Freestanding single walls render as biome props. Also draws animated door
  barriers and glyph lights.
- `tileArt.ts` / `palette.ts`: biome tiles painted with Canvas2D at load (no
  tileset images), from per-biome render palettes.
- `ActorView.ts`: sprites keyed by entity id; animation, hit flash, wind-up
  telegraphs, health bars, projectiles, pickups, chests, wells and the rift.
- `Effects.ts`: particles, slash arcs, rings, damage numbers, shake, motes.
- `sheets.ts`: cuts the sprite sheets described by `sprite_atlas.json`.

## UI (`src/ui`)

DOM elements over the canvas, styled by `ui.css`. `Hud` writes only changed
values each frame. `Screens` shows one menu at a time. `Minimap` draws visited
rooms and their neighbours to a canvas.

## Persistence (`src/save`)

`SaveStore` keeps two localStorage keys: meta progress (fragments, records,
settings), validated by a zod schema, and the run snapshot written at each
floor's entrance. Missing, corrupt or old-format data falls back to defaults;
storage errors never break the game.

- Keep `src/sim` free of DOM and PixiJS imports, so it stays testable headlessly.

# Game Project Principles

**This document must be read by every AI agent working on this project.**

> **Current architecture:** the module-contract, event-bus and RLM sections
> below describe the original design, which was replaced by a deterministic
> `src/sim` core with separate view, UI and app layers (ADR-016). The goals
> still apply: readable code, seeded determinism, a headless simulation,
> serializable state and layered visuals. For how they are met now, see
> [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Core Principles
- **Decision**: `CombatSystem.executePhaseAbilities` maps authored names to concrete effects: `forgotten_army` summons two echoes, `void_domain` and `true_ending` fire projectile rings, `timeline_shift` teleports to a non-solid candidate near the player, and `reconstruction_beam` fires a three-shot aimed spread; every execution emits `combat:bossAbility`. Bosses (`phases.length > 0`) are excluded from elite rolls. `PlayerSystem` tracks a `runCompleted` guard that resets on death/permadeath, and `resetRunState` clears the run inventory. Victory modal data is built by the pure `src/ui/victorySummary.ts` helper and unit-tested.
- **Consequences**: Boss phases now change the fight instead of only the stat sheet, deep bosses stay hand-tuned, run completion cannot be farmed without dying, permadeath is a complete run reset, and the victory payload is testable without a DOM. Unknown ability names still emit `combat:bossAbility` for future content instead of disappearing silently. Attack and collision loops snapshot their target collections, so phase-spawned minions cannot be hit by the same swing that triggered the phase. Damage-over-time ticks also cross phase thresholds, and the once-per-run completion guard is serialized so saving after a victory cannot re-arm it.

### ADR-012: Release-candidate stabilization gate
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The project had no CI, the in-game tutorial still described radial slashes after combat moved to a facing cone, and authored content JSON was only validated by whichever runtime module happened to import it. The README project tree also contained mojibake and omitted the gameplay catalogs and UI modules.
- **Decision**: Add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running `npm ci`, lint, typecheck, tests and the production build on pushes and pull requests. Rewrite the tutorial's core-loop text to describe the 120-degree cone, hit-confirmed combo, Memory Surge, telegraphed windups, authored loot, depth and Keeper completion. Add `tests/data.test.ts` for enemy id/stat/range invariants, loot references and quantities, descending phase thresholds, elite modifier bounds, item id/stack invariants and gameplay-config parsing. Replace the README tree with ASCII and document the CI/local pre-push gate.
- **Consequences**: Every change gets an objective remote gate, onboarding matches the simulation, and malformed content fails before playtests. The data tests intentionally validate authored invariants rather than runtime behavior, so they stay fast and do not duplicate the combat suite.

### ADR-013: Make loot usable with equipment and consumables
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Loot tables produced real items, but there was no way to use or equip them, so equipment and consumables were dead inventory weight and the tutorial could not honestly promise a loot loop.
- **Decision**: `PlayerSystem` gains `useItem`, `equipItem`, `unequipSlot`, an `EquipmentState` with weapon/armor/accessory slots, and equipment-aware derived stats. Consumables heal, restore mana, grant invincibility, convert fragment/memory value, and memory items unlock abilities. Equipment applies numeric stats (damage, armor, resistance, move speed, crit, attack speed, mana, dash cooldown/distance) on equip and removes them on unequip. Equipment is serialized and cleared by permadeath. `MenuSystem` gains an Inventory & Equipment overlay that renders equipped slots and backpack items, delegates Use/Equip/Unequip, and refreshes on inventory/equipment events.
- **Consequences**: Loot now changes the next fight, the tutorial matches the real loop, and equipment survives save/load. Player crit gear applies only to outgoing critical hits; incoming enemy crits stay on the global multiplier. Memory pickups honor authored `memoryValue` (10 per fragment item, matching the 10-shard conversion) and `fragmentValue`. The overlay is DOM-only and covered by typecheck/build; item/equipment rules are unit-tested. Items with unsimulated stats (lifesteal, regen, memory-find) still store the data but do not yet alter combat.

### ADR-014: Measure balance with deterministic duels and restore melee commitment
- **Date**: 2026-10-22
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: The new balance matrix (`BALANCE_REPORT=1`) showed a stationary level-1 player taking zero damage from every melee enemy. Two causes: ordinary light-hit knockback cancelled the enemy windup on the next AI tick, and the player's 30px offset + 60px radius gave an effective 90px reach that outranged nearly every melee enemy (40-80px). Combat had no reliable melee threat.
- **Decision**: Add `tests/balance.test.ts`, a deterministic PlayerSystem + CombatSystem duel harness with TTK/damage/hit metrics and optional matrix output. Remove `knockedBack` from the unconditional windup interrupt; only stun/freeze and explicit damage at/above `staggerThreshold` (or criticals) cancel it. Add `combat.meleeOffset` (20) and `combat.meleeRange` (35) so effective reach is 55px. This supersedes ADR-008's knockback-cancel clause.
- **Consequences**: Melee enemies now complete their commitment and can damage a stationary player; short-range enemies trade hits, while longer-reach/ranged enemies punish standing still. The balance test locks scavenger level-1 victory, determinism and Keeper impossibility at level 1. Reach and attack ranges still need live playtesting, and the stationary duel intentionally does not model dodging or movement.

### ADR-015: Overhaul procedural terrain generation, eliminate RLM frame lag, and establish Metroidvania map, inventory and skills UI
- **Date**: 2026-10-25
- **Status**: Accepted
- **Context**: Visual and performance inspection via headless browser revealed that terrain generation produced a chaotic checkerboard of floating tiles, isolated spikes, and water in mid-air due to raw non-spatial coordinate hashing in `WorldSystem.getNoise`. Furthermore, an ambient lighting graphics box attached to the effects layer in world space washed out the positive quadrant of the screen, and continuous RLM `serializeAll()` snapshots every 60 frames caused 500ms lag spikes on movement. Finally, players lacked starting equipment, hotkeys for navigation, a map/minimap, and any interface to allocate stat points or unlock/upgrade abilities.
- **Decision**: Overhaul `WorldSystem.generateTiles` with 6 deterministic room archetypes (Promenade, Stepped Ruins, Sunken Reservoir, Hazard Pit with Platforms, Twin Towers, and Altar Crypt) guaranteeing contiguous floors, level boundaries at matching heights, proper pit placement for hazards/water, and a safe starting Sanctuary. Remove the world-space ambient rectangle artifact in `RenderSystem`. Gate RLM snapshots in `AISystem.update` to active agent sessions and cull off-screen enemy rendering in `ActorRenderer`. Grant starter equipment (`Memory Blade`, `Scavenger's Vest`, `Memory Elixir` x3) on fresh runs in `PlayerSystem`. Overhaul `MenuSystem` to provide a persistent HUD minimap, full-screen World Map modal (`KeyM`), comprehensive Inventory & Equipment panel with live character sheet (`KeyI`/`KeyB`), Disciplines & Skills management panel (`KeyK`) for stat allocation and ability progression, and Settings audio/graphics controls.
- **Consequences**: Frame rates stabilize at a smooth 60.2 FPS with zero lag spikes, terrain is structured, walkable and aesthetically coherent across biomes, players can navigate with the minimap and full map, combat gear is equipped from run start, and the full RPG progression loop (attributes and abilities) is accessible and functional. All unit tests, typechecks, lint, hygiene, guidelines, and secret scans pass (7/7 gates).

content.text:
I rebuilt Memory Reconstruction as a top-down action roguelike, and it now plays from the title screen through to victory. Run `start.bat` or `npm start` to try it. I haven't committed anything; Claude Code only commits when you ask.

**What was actually wrong**
- **Graphics:** the tile art is side-on platformer art (grass-topped ground, ladders, platforms), but the game drew it from above. That's why floors looked like horizontal stripes.
- **UI:** the minimap crashed every frame, the health text drew over itself, and there was no title screen.
- **Code:** about 19,600 lines, 940 lint warnings, and 117 tests that never checked anything you see on screen.

**What it is now**
- **Floors:** six biomes, each a set of rooms. Walking into a room seals the doors until the enemies are dead. There are treasure chests, Memory Wells (spend shards to heal and get an upgrade) and a boss guarding each exit.
- **Combat:** a mouse-aimed 3-hit combo, a dash that makes you briefly invulnerable, a magic bolt that costs mana, and potions. Every enemy attack shows a red warning shape on the ground before it lands, and enemies never hurt you just by touching you. 13 enemy types and 6 bosses with three phases each.
- **Progression:** each level-up offers 3 upgrade cards from a pool of 18. Memory fragments are kept even when you die; collect a full set to unlock a story.
- **Presentation:** floor and wall tiles are painted by the game itself for each biome. The interface is a proper HTML overlay with a minimap, pause, settings and death/victory screens. All sounds and music are generated in the browser. It saves at each floor's entrance and works with a gamepad.

**How I checked it**
- 69 tests pass, and the project's 7 checks all pass, including build and lint with zero warnings.
- I played it in a real browser through every screen: chest, rift, the next floor, reload and Continue, death, memories, settings and victory. No console errors, 60 FPS.
- A bot played 40 complete runs without getting stuck anywhere. Those runs exposed real bugs I then fixed: enemies stuck behind pillars, characters snagging on wall corners, and an exit portal that sometimes wouldn't let you leave.
- I tuned difficulty with that bot. A skilled bot wins about 45% of runs and a clumsy one about 20%, with deaths mostly on floors 3–5.

**Things to know**
- **Deleted tests:** I removed the 12 test files that only covered the deleted code (`balance`, `combat`, `config`, `core`, `data`, `enemy_ai`, `mechanics`, `memory`, the old `save`, `victory`, `world`, `graphics.assets`). New tests replace them, and the decision record (ADR-016 in `.aikit/decisions.md`) names each one.
- **Removed:** five unused packages, three npm scripts pointing at files that don't exist, and the obsolete RLM checker and its doc.
- **Old saves:** saves from the old version are ignored rather than loaded.
- **`PROJECT_PRINCIPLES.md`:** I didn't rewrite your design document. I only added a short note at the top saying its module-system sections describe the old design.
- **Unused data:** the items, equipment, abilities and dialogue JSON are still there but the new game doesn't use them yet.
- **Not checked by hand:** I couldn't hear the audio or test a physical gamepad, and how the controls feel still needs a person to play it.

The previous agent's unfinished changes are saved on the `wip/topdown-qol-abandoned` branch. Want me to commit this work to `main`?
Holy shit, this is sooo good. good job, you are the man....

Thanks, glad it plays well!

Everything is still uncommitted. If you want, I can commit it to `main` as a few milestone commits: the simulation core, then the renderer and UI, then polish and docs.

Things I'd look at next, if you want to keep going:

- **Feel:** play a few runs yourself. Damage, dash timing and how often enemies attack are easy to tweak, and the bot can't judge whether it's fun.
- **Unused content:** the items, abilities and dialogue JSON could become shop items, chest rewards or NPCs at the Memory Wells.
- **More variety:** room layouts beyond the current pillar patterns, more upgrade cards, or a second weapon type.
